newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia says agrees electricity deal with Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia says agrees electricity deal with Croatia.

text.p: The Bosnian state power company said on Friday it signed an agreement with Croatian representatives to supply electricity to Croatia.
Elektroprivreda planned to provide 320 kilowatt hours of electricity to Croatia, which amounts to nine percent of Bosnia's total power production, General Manager Emir Aganovic told reporters.
The Croatian electricity board (HEP) agreed to pay Elektroprivreda for 60 percent of the electricity in cash and the remainder in mining and power plant equipment, he said.
Company officials offered no estimate of how much the deal was worth but hailed the agreement as a sign of improving economic ties between the two countries.
"This agreement is the first step in resuming co-operation between the two countries," Aganovic said.
Industrial and transport links between Bosnia and Croatia were disrupted by the violent disintegration of old Yugoslavia beginning in 1991.
HEP director, Damir Begovic, said Croatia also agreed in principle to revive investment in thermoelectric plants in the Bosnian towns of Tuzla and Kakanj.
The United States Agency for International Development has donated some $24 million to repair two generators at the Kakanj power plant.
